title: Russia, Ukraine, Turkey and the UN sign the Black Sea Grain Initiative in Istanbul
body:
The Black Sea Grain Initiative was signed on 22 July 2022 at Dolmabahce Palace in Istanbul, Turkey. The parties were Ukraine, Russia, Turkey and the United Nations; Ukraine and Russia signed separate mirror agreements with Turkey and the UN rather than a direct bilateral deal. The original term was 120 days, and a Joint Coordination Centre in Istanbul with 20 delegates, five from each party, oversaw inspection of ships.

Before the war Ukraine supplied more than 45 million tonnes of grain annually to global markets, and about 20 million tonnes were held up in Odesa before the deal. By mid-July 2023 nearly 33 million tonnes of grain and other food products had left Ukrainian ports, according to the Wikipedia article. The UN World Food Programme shipped over 725,200 tonnes of grain, and 57 percent of grain exports went to developing countries. In 2022 Turkey received the most shipments (170), followed by Spain (100) and Italy (81).

Russia suspended its participation on 29 October 2022 after a drone attack on Sevastopol and resumed on 2 November 2022. The deal was extended in November 2022 for 120 days, in March 2023 for at least 60 days and in May 2023 for 60 days. On 17 July 2023 Russia did not renew it, and Kremlin spokesman Dmitry Peskov said the initiative had been suspended.
